message.reasoning_content: We need to determine appropriate criminal charges based on facts. The scenario: Defendant Wang's wife made a statement at police station. Wang and his wife go to police station, tear up the statement, try to leave. Police try to stop, ask Wang to go to investigation area. Wang refuses, resists, struggles, shouts, attempts to escape, causing police officer Gao's right hand skin abrasions and right 6th rib fracture. The injury is light injury (轻微伤). The police officer is a civil servant. The act is assault on a police officer, causing injury. Also destruction of police documents (the statement). Likely charges: (1) Assault (故意伤害) of a police officer? Actually the injury is caused by Wang's violent resistance. That is "故意伤害罪" (intentional injury) because he caused injury to a police officer. However the injury is light, but still counts. Also "妨害公务罪" (obstructing public duty) because he resisted police, assaulted them, causing injury. In examples, similar case: earlier example with dangerous driving and assault on police: they gave "危险驾驶;妨害公务". That case had biting police. So here we have assault on police causing injury, plus obstruction of duty. Also "毁灭证据" maybe? He destroyed the statement (a police document). That could be "毁灭证据罪". But typical Chinese criminal law: "妨害公务罪" includes resisting, assaulting, or obstructing police in performance of duty. It covers violent resistance. Also "故意伤害罪" is separate if injury inflicted. In many cases, both charges can be applied. In examples, they sometimes list both: e.g., earlier example: "故意伤害;编造、故意传播虚假恐怖信息". Another: "故意伤害;诈骗". So we can list both "故意伤害" and "妨害公务". Also maybe "毁灭证据" but not sure if typical. The act of tearing up the statement is destroying police document, which is a crime of "毁灭证据罪". However the main focus is assault and obstruction. In similar example: "危害公共安全" etc. The examples include "妨害公务" when assaulting police. So answer: [罪名]故意伤害;妨害公务<eoa>
